name: Vitalshield-OG
description: Vitalshield-OG is a structured composite of carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer and a dense living tissue layer — a BioForge-engineered dermis analog seeded with clotting proteins, regenerative stem-cell clusters, and a capillary network that draws metabolic energy from the wearer's own circulatory system via subcutaneous interface points. Damage to the outer carbon-polymer layer triggers the tissue layer beneath to begin laying down new structural polymer precursors, with full minor-damage repair cycling in 8-16 hours during rest periods. It is the closest thing to biological armor that current materials science can produce.
applications: body armor for elite security and military personnel
protective outer sheathing for augment exteriors
combat suit underlayer for Tier 4-5 operators
cost: Φ85,000 per fitted suit (torso coverage); Φ12,000 per panel (replacement); ongoing metabolic cost equivalent to ~15% increased caloric demand on wearer
story_hooks: A Vitalshield-OG suit separated from its owner is dying — the tissue layer is necrotic without a metabolic host — but a desperate Tier 1 scavenger is trying to keep it alive by feeding it blood, not understanding what they have.

A soldier wearing Vitalshield-OG for eighteen consecutive months without proper interface maintenance has developed a condition where the suit's tissue layer has begun interfacing with their own subcutaneous tissue — the suit is slowly becoming part of their body.

An assassin discovers their target's Vitalshield-OG suit is recording biomarker data from its wearer and has been transmitting health and stress telemetry to a third party for months — someone has been monitoring the target's physiological state in real time.
